newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault seeks 10-10.5 pct Europe mkt share.
newsitem.headline: Renault seeks 10-10.5 pct Europe mkt share.

text.p: French carmaker Renault aims to capture between 10 and 10.5 percent of western European car sales in 1997, sales director Patrick Faure said on Monday.
The company's market share slipped in 1996 to 10.1 percent from 10.3 percent the previous year.

Faure told a news conference the group expected European car sales to rise slightly in 1997 as a result of a rebate incentive scheme introduced in Italy. Before the scheme was announced, the group had expected a flat European car market, he said.
Renault officials said the French car market is expected to shrink to around 1.9 million units from 2.13 million in 1996.
The company aims to increase its market share in France to around 27-28 percent from 26.6 percent in 1996, Faure said. Its share was 29.2 percent in 1995.
"1997 will be the year of the reconquest," he said. "We have the products, the strategy and the sales team to do it."
He said the group hoped the Megane car, ranked fourth in its segment in 1996 after the Volkswagen Golf, Opel Astra and Ford Escort, would be among the top three in 1997.
In addition to its French and European market share objectives, the group hopes to recoup market share in Italy.

"With the recovery of the lira, we can sell cars in Italy without losing money," Faure said. But he said the group would not take extremely aggressive measures to gain share in the Italian market, expected to benefit from the rebate scheme.
"As in France, the programme will probably skew sales toward smaller cars which isn't positive for carmakers' financial results," he said.

Overall, "our strategy is not to gain market share at any cost -- not just out of principle, but because we don't have the means," Faure said. He said there were no indications that the price war in Europe was winding down.
Renault's objective is to increase prices by a maximum of one percent in 1997, Faure said. That includes a 2,000 franc ($378) increase in the price of the Megane, set on January 1.
Faure said the truck activity faces a tough year ahead of the renewal of some products in the range at the end of 1997.

"It'll be difficult. Some of our models are older than their competitors," he said. Renault's share of the European industrial vehicle market fell to 13.7 percent in 1996 from 15.3 percent. Faure said it is aiming for 13.5 percent share in 1997.
-- Christine Tierney, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.290 French Francs)
